verdict.rationale: OpenCode's `permission` config lets admins decide whether actions (including tool calls) auto-run, prompt, or are blocked, and MCP servers (the mechanism for adding external tools) are explicitly configurable per-project; enterprise docs also describe centralizing config so all users only reach an approved internal AI gateway. This gives an engineering lead real control over external tool/integration access, though evidence is docs-only with no independent verification of granular per-tool/per-MCP-server allow-listing in practice. Missing for 10: hands-on/independent confirmation that permission rules can precisely restrict individual MCP servers or third-party integrations, and more detail on enforcement scope beyond built-in actions.
